meta.note: Fifth measurement pass (harness v2). Three changes make the harness model the two-store design in 05-per-bucket-store-design.md rather than an approximation: (a) retired node_append_large and disk_large, which used 256 KiB values under sequential position keys with a per-batch fsync - a load that exists nowhere in the design; (b) added the dedup lookup every upload performs before storing a chunk, reported as content_store extra.miss_latency and timed outside the ingest window so ingest stays comparable; (c) corrected SQLite's sync mapping from wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) per batch to a commit at synchronous=FULL, which is what the commitment store runs in production. (c) also fixed a fairness bug: the shared-architecture SQLite writer had been ignoring the sync flag entirely, which is what produced pass 4's retracted 'shared is 24x faster' result. All eight engines, disk-backed scratch (/var/tmp), one process per engine, merged by scripts/merge-db-bench-results.py. NOT comparable record-for-record with passes 1-4.
